title: Bunk Johnson's humor and the sincerity of itinerant performers
summary: Bunk was jovial and funny; she recalls minstrels, medicine shows and vaudeville that played Lake Charles for a single day with great humor and love of the work.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: What kind of a person was he?

He was a very nice man and very jovial, very, very humorous, very humorous man. I can remember he used to keep everybody laughing all the time with these old jokes. You know, one of the most marvelous things that I can remember about people like Bunk Johnson, Pat, you know, one of the most wonderful things that I can remember is to have worked around people with humor, with a sense of humor. For instance, in our little town we used to have -- the minstrels used to come there. They wouldn't play but one day, they couldn't afford to stay in a little town like Lake Charles but one day. Then we used to have the medicine shows to come there.
John Chilton's Who's Who In Jazz.

Then we used to have the vaudeville shows to come, you know, to Lake Charles. But they would all come there and maybe they would just play one day, it was a one nighter. What I'm saying is the humor, and these people weren't, you know, they weren't making any money, so to speak, just barely existing really, but the marvelous sense of humor and the love of what they did was so marvelous, and this sort of always -- it impressed me and it helped me to know that when I saw these people performing or saw them playing, like for instance Bunk Johnson, I knew that they were real sincere in what they were doing.
